clue.text: An ecstasy pill? American injected disulfiram

indicators.note: injected means the American abbreviation is pushed into the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: a tab is a slang word for a tablet or pill
E is the street abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an American was injected with a drug, perhaps an ecstasy pill.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface splits 'ecstasy pill' as one drug; in the parse the pill is TAB and ecstasy is E, which follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Antabuse is the trade name of disulfiram, a drug that makes alcohol unpleasant to drink.

clue.text: Perhaps ladies name foolish person

parts.note: a ladies' toilet is one example of a loo

explanation.surface: Someone suggests the women present might call some idiot by name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladies' is British for a women's toilet, so it is an example of LOO, signalled by 'Perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: A loon is an informal word for a crazy or silly person, a synonym for a fool.

clue.text: Heard she was seduced by swan songs?

indicators.note: heard tells us the word is taken by its sound, as if spoken

parts.note: in Greek myth Leda was seduced by Zeus in the form of a swan

explanation.surface: A question about the songs one heard of a swan's seduction, perhaps a tale set to music.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent LEDA and LIEDER are said alike, 'leeder'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieder are German art songs, typically for solo voice and piano, as by Schubert.

clue.text: Diplomatic set-up, maybe, getting worried about Nazi force

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the Nazi force
getting worried suggests the letters of the word maybe are agitated into a new order

parts.note: the SS was the Nazi paramilitary force

explanation.surface: A diplomatic arrangement, perhaps, grows anxious over the threat of Nazi forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' looks like a hedge on the definition but is the anagram fodder, giving EMBAY round SS.
explanation.definitionFit: An embassy is the establishment of an ambassador and staff, a diplomatic mission abroad.

clue.text: Live NBC broadcast with interruption from Institute that may be overcome

indicators.note: with interruption from means a letter breaks into the rearranged letters
broadcast in the sense of scattered, so the letters of Live NBC are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A live television transmission on NBC is cut into by some institute's announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like television talk but here scatters LIVE NBC.
explanation.definitionFit: Vincible is the rare opposite of invincible: capable of being conquered or defeated.

clue.text: I can do job on farm after years travelled

indicators.note: after places the farm job behind the years

parts.note: a can is a tin container
an era is a span of years
to ted is to spread out mown grass to dry for hay

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that after many years they can still manage farm work.
explanation.walkthrough: TED, a farming verb meaning to turn hay, is the 'job on farm'.
explanation.definitionFit: To itinerate is to journey from place to place, as a circuit preacher or judge does.

clue.text: Rope, tethered initially further up, causes singular admiration

indicators.note: further up, in a down clue, means that letter is shifted higher in the word

parts.note: a lariat is a lasso or rope

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the word tethered

explanation.surface: A rope tethered high up draws particular praise.
explanation.walkthrough: The T of LARIAT moves up two places to give LATRIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Latria is the supreme worship owed to God alone, adoration that is unique or singular.

clue.text: I'll step in once poor mother's given eulogy

indicators.note: step in means the single letter enters among the other pieces
poor suggests the word once is in bad shape and so reshuffled

parts.note: mum is an informal word for mother
the letter I is taken from I'll

explanation.surface: A speaker volunteers to step in to deliver the eulogy, since poor Mum once did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' makes ENCO from 'once'; 'I'll step in' puts I just after the first letter of the mother.
explanation.definitionFit: An encomium is a formal speech or piece of writing that praises someone highly.

clue.text: Missing the odd signature, any papers here?

definitions.text: Missing the odd signature, any papers here?

indicators.note: missing the odd means dropping the odd-placed letters and keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: An office worker hunting for a stray signed document asks whether any papers are waiting here.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep the even letters of 'signature any', counting straight across both words, to get I N T R A Y.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-tray is the desk tray where incoming papers wait, the natural place to look for documents.

clue.text: Conceited streak in one's nature we've picked up

indicators.note: picked up as in heard by ear, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a vein is a trait or strain running through someone's character

explanation.surface: We have noticed a conceited trait running through someone's character.
explanation.definitionFit: Vain describes someone with an excessive pride in their looks or achievements, a synonym of conceited.

clue.text: Fantastic deed involving Cretan Bull

indicators.note: fantastic in the sense of fanciful or wild, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An amazing exploit involving the Cretan Bull, one of the labours of Hercules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bull' looks like part of the mythical beast but is the definition: a bull's-eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A bull is short for bull's-eye, the exact middle of a target.

clue.text: On a mission to get orders to 4

indicators.note: orders as a verb, arranges, so the letters are put in a new sequence

parts.note: the number 4 written as a word

explanation.surface: Someone on a mission carries instructions to the embassy of entry 4.
explanation.walkthrough: The '4' looks like a cross-reference to 4 down but is simply the word FOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out for something means setting out determined to obtain it.

clue.text: Looking up poem suitable for singing, it's hard to accept 50% of that is loaded

indicators.note: looking up, in a down clue, means the poem's title is read from the bottom

parts.note: If is Kipling's famous poem

indicators.note: to accept means the first pieces open up to take in another

parts.note: lyric means suited to being sung

indicators.note: 50% of means half the word that, its first two letters

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Reading up a poem fit to be sung, one finds it hard to take in half of something loaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looking up poem' is IF read upward, FI, which leads; LYRIC + H then takes in TH, half of 'that'.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaded is slang for extremely wealthy, someone with a great deal of money.

clue.text: Provincial old City Underground off limits with this?

parts.note: sub is short for subway, an underground railway
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
a ban puts something off limits

explanation.surface: A question whether an old City of London tube station should be closed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City Underground' reads as the London Tube, but UR is the ancient city and SUB the underground.
explanation.definitionFit: Suburban can mean narrow-minded or parochial, like provincial in its pejorative sense.

clue.text: A possible pathway to the west, zilch in left sphere of vision

indicators.note: to the west, in an across clue, means the letters run right to left
in means the nothing goes inside the eye

parts.note: the eye is the ball, or sphere, with which we see
zilch is slang for nil or nothing

explanation.surface: Something about a path westward, with nothing appearing on the left of one's view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts zilch inside the eye to make ENILYE, which 'to the west' turns to EYLINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ley line is a supposed alignment of ancient sites, said by some to mark an old track.

clue.text: Little number — it turns Nimrod on before 12!

indicators.note: before places the word on ahead of the turned pieces

parts.note: no. is the short form of number

indicators.note: turns means the word it is turned round

parts.note: Nimrod, the setter, refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A short song that excites the setter, timed to finish before twelve.
explanation.walkthrough: Nimrod is the setter's pseudonym, so he is ME; IT turns to TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve o'clock midday is noon, the time of day this word names.

clue.text: Spot Psammead's name written backwards in blocks

indicators.note: in means the other letters go inside the toy blocks

parts.note: Lego is the brand of interlocking toy building blocks

indicators.note: written backwards means the creature's name is read in reverse

parts.note: the Psammead is the sand-fairy of Nesbit's Five Children and It, called It

explanation.surface: A child spots the Psammead's name spelled backwards in toy bricks.
explanation.definitionFit: Lentigo is a small flat brown spot on the skin, such as a freckle.

clue.text: After loss of one, point's my lowest

indicators.note: the 's stands for has, so the shortened word holds the next piece
after loss of means a letter is taken out of the word for point

parts.note: the gist is the main point of something
I is the Roman numeral for one
lumme is an exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'

explanation.surface: Someone says that after losing one game this is their worst moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After loss of one' leaves GST; the 's stands for 'has', so it holds the Cockney cry of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Glum means dejected, so its superlative means the most downcast, the least cheerful.

clue.text: Swearing private statement about compressing oxygen

indicators.note: compressing means the turned word squeezes another letter inside
about means the word statement is turned round

parts.note: a report is an account or statement
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A private announcement concerning compressed oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: TROPER (REPORT turned 'about') closes round O after its third letter. A trooper is a cavalry private, proverbially foul-mouthed.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear like a trooper is the idiom, so a trooper is the private soldier noted for oaths.

clue.text: Boat en route from Buckfastleigh to Arundel

indicators.note: en route means the answer lies along the way, within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A boat travelling between two English towns, Buckfastleigh in Devon and Arundel in Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: An eight-oar is a rowing boat for eight oarsmen, a racing eight.

clue.text: Italy's not at all good at services

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy
bad is the opposite of good

explanation.surface: Italy is poor at providing services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'services' suggests trade, but means religious observances.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibadat are Islamic acts of worship, religious duties such as prayer and fasting.

clue.text: Dislike being on Holmes' tail? It's elementary

indicators.note: being on places the dislike after that letter
tail picks the final letter of the detective's name

parts.note: odium is strong dislike or hatred

explanation.surface: Hating to be followed while tailing Holmes, with a nod to 'Elementary, my dear Watson'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodium is a chemical element, so it is literally elementary.

clue.text: Bruce working on farm — and inside of cheese shop

definitions.text: Bruce working on farm — and inside of cheese shop

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are set in motion and rearranged, as on a busy farm
inside of picks the two central letters of the word cheese

explanation.surface: An Australian, Bruce, works on a farm and also inside a cheese shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of cheese is EE; with SHOP, rearranged by working, it makes SHEEPO. The whole clue paints the Australian farmhand, Bruce being the stock Australian name.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian usage a sheepo is a shed hand who penned the flock for the shearers.

clue.text: Risk other suffering, overstepping a very fine line

indicators.note: overstepping means the rearranged letters stride over the single letter, holding it
suffering suggests the words are damaged and so rearranged

explanation.surface: Taking risks with another's suffering crosses a very fine line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overstepping a very fine line' reads as one phrase, but 'a' is fodder held inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairstroke is a very thin stroke in writing or type, a hairline.

clue.text: Scots carry a lot out of Falmouth, bit by bit to get sent back

indicators.note: sent back means the remaining letters are read in reverse
out of, with bit by bit, means those letters are removed one at a time from the place name

explanation.surface: Scotsmen haul a great deal away from Falmouth, the Cornish port, piece by piece, to be returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit by bit' says A, L, O, T leave Falmouth separately, leaving FMUH.
explanation.definitionFit: Humf is a Scottish dialect form of hump, meaning to carry or lug something heavy.

clue.text: People who modernise dresses

indicators.note: dresses as in clothes, the outer words wrapping the answer

explanation.surface: Those who bring things up to date are clothing designers.
explanation.definitionFit: Homo is the genus of humans, so it stands for people as a biological group.

clue.text: Morning application: a short letter of credit accepted by corporation

indicators.note: accepted by means the letters are taken inside the belly

parts.note: corporation is old slang for a paunch, so a tum or belly
LC is the abbreviation for letter of credit

explanation.surface: A morning bank application for a short letter of credit, accepted by the corporation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' looks like a company but is a jokey old word for a pot belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Talcum powder is dusted on after washing, a typical part of a morning routine.

clue.text: Order some soup and a sparkling wine

indicators.note: order as a verb, arrange, so the letters are put in a new sequence

explanation.surface: A restaurant diner asks for soup and a glass of fizz.
explanation.definitionFit: Espumoso is Spanish or Portuguese sparkling wine.
